solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shimmering sapphire emitting one, maybe

indicators.note: something shimmering shifts and flickers, so these letters are to be rearranged
emitting means giving out, so the letter for one leaves the pool before rearranging

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A jewel catches the light and gives off a gleam, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emitting' takes I out of SAPPHIRE, and 'Shimmering' rearranges the seven letters left, SAPPHRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are adverbs expressing possibility rather than certainty, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Brag, perhaps, to follow having this collection of suits

definitions.text: Brag, perhaps, to follow having this collection of suits

parts.words: Brag, perhaps, to follow having this collection of suits
parts.note: brag is a card game, and you can only follow suit in it if you have the full set of fifty-two; 'collection of suits' sounds like a wardrobe of clothes

explanation.surface: Boasting about a wardrobe full of tailored suits.
explanation.walkthrough: Brag is a British card game related to poker; to play it, or to follow suit, you need the deck of hearts, clubs, diamonds and spades.
explanation.definitionFit: A full deck holds four suits, and games such as brag need one before anyone can play.

clue.text: Shipyard work, note, falling into current

definitions.note: the clue names the job; the solver supplies the person doing that shipyard work

indicators.note: falling into means dropping inside, so the note goes within the word for current

parts.note: a river is a current of flowing water
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A dockyard task interrupted when a musical note drops into a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names the trade by its work; the answer is the worker who hammers metal pins through ship plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships were built by hammering hot metal pins through steel plates, the job of a specialist yard tradesman.

clue.text: Lorry that man used to transport satisfactory vegetable

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, British for a semi-trailer truck

indicators.note: to transport something is to carry it inside, so the pronoun holds the next piece

parts.note: that man is he
OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: A man drives a lorry delivering an acceptable vegetable crop.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTIC is British slang for an articulated lorry (a semi-trailer truck).
explanation.definitionFit: A globe artichoke is an edible thistle bud, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Drink in excess initially has you laid out

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word excess

explanation.surface: Overindulging in drink leaves you flat on your back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying face upward, stretched flat, is the posture of someone laid out.

clue.text: Head of kitchen first to lose heart

indicators.note: losing heart means dropping the central letter of the word for first

parts.note: chief means first or foremost

explanation.surface: A head cook is the first to grow discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose heart' removes I, the middle letter of CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: The cook in charge of a restaurant kitchen holds this title, which comes from French for boss.

clue.text: Vehicle offering endless concern

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter of the word for concern

parts.note: care means concern or worry

explanation.surface: A vehicle that brings constant worry to its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor vehicle for the road is the commonest example of the general term.

clue.text: Queen interrupting peer, though not right peer

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the queen abbreviation sits inside the noble
not right means the R, for right, is taken out

parts.note: an earl is a British peer, a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A queen cuts in on a nobleman, but the second peer is the wrong one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' appears twice: the first is a nobleman, the second the definition. 'though not right' removes R, and 'interrupting' puts the queen inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is someone of the same standing or rank as another, one's match.

clue.text: Want business to take on old soldier

indicators.note: taking on means adding, so the soldier follows the business

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
vet, short for veteran, is an old soldier

explanation.surface: A firm short of staff wants to hire an ex-serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something that belongs to someone else is a strong kind of wanting.

clue.text: Runs into vicious person with power, retreating in shock

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the rest
retreating means going backwards, so the brute and power are read in reverse

parts.note: a brute is a vicious person
P is the physics symbol for power
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone flees from a powerful thug, in a state of shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns BRUTE + P into PETURB; 'into' then puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock someone is to unsettle or disturb them, the verb's core meaning.

clue.text: Arts bloomed with revival in circulation

indicators.note: a revival gives the letters new life in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: The arts flourished again as a renaissance came into circulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood moving round the body is its circulation, the flow through the vessels.

clue.text: Dismissed in contest, though not bowled

indicators.note: not means the letter for bowled is removed

parts.note: a bout is a contest, as in boxing
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: A cricketer is given out in a match without being bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman can be dismissed without being bowled, e.g. caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman dismissed in cricket is said to be no longer in, the standard term.

clue.text: Against end of recital being given to singer

parts.note: contra is Latin for against

indicators.note: end of points to the final letter of the word recital

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to the close of a concert being handed to a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest female voice in a choir names the performer who sings that part.

clue.text: Trustworthy theatre board accommodating Feydeau's last

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
a table is a board, as in board and lodging

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of Feydeau's name

explanation.surface: A dependable theatre company's board stages Feydeau's final farce.
explanation.walkthrough: Georges Feydeau was a French writer of farces; only his name's final letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone of good standing and reliable character is trustworthy.

clue.text: Screen feature not entirely superficial

indicators.note: not entirely means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: cursory means superficial or hasty

explanation.surface: An aspect of a display that runs deeper than appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the Y from CURSORY.
explanation.definitionFit: The movable pointer shown on a computer display is part of what a screen shows.

clue.text: Raving aloud about quiet addition to website?

definitions.note: the clue gives the item added; the answer can be a noun for such an item

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes round the quiet letter
raving means wild and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone shouts loudly about a muted new post on a site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raving' rearranges ALOUD to ULOAD, and 'about' puts it round P.
explanation.definitionFit: A file sent from a user's computer up to a server is a new item added to the site.

clue.text: Casual worker not working at first

indicators.note: at first places the not-working piece ahead of the worker

parts.note: off means not working, as a switched-off machine
a hand is a worker, as a farmhand

explanation.surface: A casual labourer is idle to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual, careless manner is the same as an offhand one: brusque and unconcerned.

clue.text: The French aristocrat given a pardon

parts.note: le is French for the
toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A French nobleman receives a pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone excused from punishment is released without penalty, the phrasal-verb sense.

clue.text: Salesman to begrudge exhibit

parts.note: rep, a sales representative, is a salesman
to resent is to begrudge

explanation.surface: A sales rep is meant to resent the display.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand for or display something is to show it, as an exhibit does.

clue.text: Scotsman engaged in musical work, turning up this instrument

indicators.note: engaged in means occupied within, so the Scotsman goes inside
turning up means reading upwards in a down entry, so the work is reversed

parts.note: op, opus, is a numbered musical work
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Scot takes part in a performance and turns up with this instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' works because this is a down entry, read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard instrument with hammers striking strings, named from the Italian for soft.

clue.text: Healthy if faint on odd occasions

indicators.note: on odd occasions picks the first, third and fifth letters of the word faint

explanation.surface: Someone well sometimes feels light-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in good physical condition is the same as being healthy.

clue.text: Cleaner, fake, not entirely substandard

parts.note: sham means fake

indicators.note: not entirely means the final letter is left off

parts.note: poor means substandard

explanation.surface: A counterfeit cleaning product of rather low quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the R from POOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid soap for washing hair is a cleaner, a cleaning product.

clue.text: Favourite exercises taking brief time

indicators.note: taking means adding on, so the time letter is attached

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A preferred workout that takes only a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher's favoured pupil is a darling, the most-liked one.

clue.text: Line presented in unadorned sound of horn

indicators.note: presented in means placed inside, so the line goes within

parts.note: bare means plain, unadorned

explanation.surface: A melody played plainly on the horn.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud harsh noise, as from a car horn or trumpet, is the word's meaning.

clue.text: What fills all of this room?

indicators.note: what fills these words lies inside them, spanning their letters

explanation.surface: A riddle: what could fill this entire room?
explanation.walkthrough: 'What fills' points inside ALL OF THIS, where the room sits across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic or upper storey under a roof is a type of room.

clue.text: Liberty from having to go round ebbing river

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the word from encloses the river
ebbing means flowing back, so the river is reversed

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Escaping from having to walk round a river at low tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is taken literally as letters, not as a link word, despite reading like one.
explanation.definitionFit: The two words share the sense of being free, unconstrained, synonyms.
